title: Managing Stress
text: Stress is a normal response to demands. Short-term stress can help people focus. Ongoing stress may affect sleep, mood, and concentration. Noticing early signs such as muscle tension, irritability, or racing thoughts helps people choose a helpful response sooner.

title: Anxiety Disorders
text: Anxiety becomes a clinical concern when worry is intense, lasting, and interferes with daily life. Cognitive behavioural approaches often help people identify unhelpful thoughts, test them against evidence, and practise gradual exposure to avoided situations.

title: PTSD Basics
text: Post-traumatic stress can include re-experiencing, avoidance, negative changes in mood or thinking, and heightened arousal. Evidence-based therapies include trauma-focused cognitive behavioural therapy and prolonged exposure when clinically appropriate.

title: Rethinking Drinking
text: People can track drinks, set limits, and plan for high-risk situations. Motivation, social support, and skills for refusing drinks are common workbook themes. Seek medical advice for withdrawal risk before stopping heavy use abruptly.
